newsitem.title: UGANDA: Mandela calls for action on African problems.
newsitem.headline: Mandela calls for action on African problems.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Wednesday challenged Africans to quickly tackle the poorest continent's endless problems of war, poverty and disease.
Mandela, in Uganda to attend the East African country's independence annivesary, also thanked Ugandans for their "selfless support" for his struggle against apartheid
The South African leader said the end of apartheid racial segregation in his country gave Africa an opportunity to look at its own future and confront its many challenges.

"Now that our continent has brought itself to the point at which it can indeed make its own future, the challenges confont us with urgency," Mandela told thousands of Ugandans who included his host President Yoweri Museveni.

"Despite the fabulous wealth of its resources Africa is threatened by marginalization within the world economy. Lasting peace still evades us," he said, pointing to the war-torn examples of Rwanda, Burundi, Liberia and Somalia.

Mandela promised to use his and South Africa's influence to help find a solution to ethnic conflict in the tiny central African nation of Burundi, where the Tutsi-dominated army is waging war against Hutu rebels.

"It was in pursuit of this commitment that South Africa appointed a special representive to support the efforts of the East African leaders in finding a peaceful political solution to the crisis in Burundi.

"Only the success of such collective efforts to resolve conflicts, and still more of measures to prevent conflicts, will create the conditions for the sustained development that will banish poverty, hunger and disease," he added.
East African leaders will meet in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha over the weekend to review policy on Burundi, reeling under sanctions they imposed last July.
On the bilateral front, Mandela promised Museveni his country would soon open a diplomatic mission in Uganda.
"I am very pleased to be able to say that Uganda's diplomatic mission in Pretoria will quite soon be matched by a South African diplomatic mission in Kampala," he said.

Wearing his trade-mark multi-coloured shirt and limping from an operation last month on his leg, Mandela later told a news conference his country would reciprocate help received from Uganda during South Africa's fight against white minority rule.
"Uganda was one of the strongest supporters of the ANC (Africa National Congress) struggle," he said.
Mandela, who has come under criticism for rolling out the red carpet for Iranian, Libyan and Cuban leaders, defended the action saying those countries helped him fight against white rule.
"Those who were with us when we were alone we never forget, whatever others say. Even though they might have many enemies, we look at them as our friends," he said.
